justification: Panel A depicts a winged human-headed figure and a bearded winged deity in profile with wings, muscular naturalistic rendering, and feathered garments, engaged in a confrontational pose, while panel B depicts a single frontal humanoid figure encased in dense geometric and symbolic ornamentation on a vertical stela, in a completely different stylistic idiom (blocky, glyphic, layered masks rather than naturalistic anatomy). The only broad commonality is that both show an upright figure with a human-like face, but the forms, postures, attributes (wings, weapons vs. masks, headdress panels) and compositional arrangement are entirely different, so there is no specific shared iconographic scheme.
